content.text:
The dashboard and the alert rule are both in Kibana, and the rule is enabled. I read both back from Kibana to confirm they exist. The rule has already run once without errors and is not firing yet.

**1. What the data holds.** `kibana_sample_data_logs` has about 14,000 web requests. The time field is `timestamp`, and the data runs from 4 Oct to 3 Dec 2026, so part of it is dated in the future. Each request records:
- the response code, bytes sent, host, URL and request;
- the client IP, user agent and machine OS;
- source and destination countries and map coordinates.

Only three response codes appear:

| Code | Requests | Avg bytes |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | 12,832 | ~5.9 KB |
| 404 | 801 | ~5.0 KB |
| 503 | 441 | 0 |

So the only server errors (5xx) in this data are 503s, and they carry no data.

**2. Dashboard: "EFF-bf925d79 Web logs overview".** It's at http://localhost:15601/app/dashboards#/view/eff-bf925d79-web-logs-overview-362eb9ba4604 and has 7 panels:
- three single numbers: total requests, unique visitors (counted by client IP) and total bytes served;
- requests over time, split by response code;
- a pie chart of response codes;
- a table of the top 10 URLs, with request count and bytes;
- the top 10 source countries.

The default time range is the last 7 days through 60 days ahead, so the future-dated records show up.

**3. Alert rule: "EFF-bf925d79 5xx spike"** (id `37eabe93-59f6-4fcb-a0a6-3b5200d519db`).
- It runs every minute and counts requests whose response code starts with "5".
- It fires when there are more than 10 in the last 5 minutes.
- It's tagged `EFF-bf925d79`.

The rule has no actions attached, so when it fires it only records an alert in Kibana and doesn't notify anyone. If you want Slack or email notifications, a connector needs to be set up and added to the rule.
